name_en: Botan nabe — wild boar and vegetable hot pot in a miso broth
summary_ja: 白と赤の合わせみそでとっただしに、猪肉と季節の野菜をたっぷり入れて煮る丹波篠山の鍋。粉山椒を効かせて食べることが多く、切り分けた猪肉を牡丹の花びらのように盛り付ける店もあるという。
summary_en: A Tanba-Sasayama hot pot of wild boar and seasonal vegetables simmered in a broth of white and red miso, often finished with a dusting of ground Japanese pepper. Some restaurants are said to arrange the sliced boar meat like the petals of a peony.
source_publisher: 農林水産省「うちの郷土料理」

name_en: Chobojiru — a sweet-free dumpling soup with cowpeas and taro-stem, made for new mothers
summary_ja: とろりとしただし汁にささげ豆と里芋の茎、もち粉の団子を煮た淡路島の汁もの。甘くはないが汁粉に似た見た目で、産後の女性の体力回復や子どものお宮参りの祝いに作られてきたという。
summary_en: An Awaji Island soup of cowpeas, taro-stem, and rice-flour dumplings simmered in a thick broth — it looks like a sweet red bean soup but is not sweet at all. It has been made to help new mothers recover and to mark a child's shrine visit, it is said.
source_publisher: 農林水産省「うちの郷土料理」

name_en: Kasujiru — a root vegetable soup simmered with sake lees
summary_ja: 大根やニンジン、ゴボウなどを日本酒の酒粕でじっくり煮込んだ汁もの。灘の酒どころを抱える兵庫県では酒粕が身近だったとされ、正月明けの一月二十日に鮭や鰤の残り骨からだしをとって食べる風習が伝わる。
summary_en: A soup of daikon, carrot, and burdock simmered slowly with sake lees. Hyogo, home to the Nada sake-brewing district, is said to have long had lees close at hand, and a custom survives of making it on January 20th with stock drawn from leftover salmon or yellowtail bones.
source_publisher: 農林水産省「うちの郷土料理」

name_en: Hamo-suki — conger pike eel and Awaji onion simmered in a seasoned broth
summary_ja: 骨切りしたハモと淡路島産タマネギを、だし汁で煮ながら食べる寄せ鍋。沼島近海の泥地で育つハモは皮が薄くやわらかいとされ、脂がのる初夏から秋にかけて、玉ねぎの甘みと合わせて味わう。
summary_en: A hot pot of bone-cut conger pike eel and Awaji Island onion simmered together in a seasoned broth. Eel from the muddy waters near Numashima is said to have thin, tender skin, and the dish is eaten from early summer through autumn as the fish takes on fat and pairs with the onion's sweetness.
source_publisher: 農林水産省「うちの郷土料理」

name_en: Kajiya nabe — octopus and eggplant simmered in a sweet soy broth, a blacksmiths' dish
summary_ja: だし汁に醤油とみりんで甘辛く味付けし、タコとナスを煮込む三木市の鍋。金物の町で働く鍛冶職人がほてった体を冷やすために食べたと伝わり、行商が運んできた明石沖のタコと夏野菜のナスを合わせている。
summary_en: A Miki City hot pot of octopus and eggplant simmered in a sweet soy broth. It is said to have been eaten by the town's blacksmiths, known for its metalware, to cool down after working the forge, combining octopus brought by traveling vendors from the Akashi coast with summer eggplant.
source_publisher: 農林水産省「うちの郷土料理」

name_en: Saba no jau — a mackerel and vegetable hot pot cooked fisherman-style
summary_ja: サバを三枚におろし、頭と骨でとっただしに身と白菜、春菊、焼き豆腐を入れてすき焼き風に煮る但馬地域の漁師めし。豊岡市竹野などサバの水揚げが多い港町で食べられてきたとされ、漁から戻った朝に食べることもあった。
summary_en: A fisherman's dish from the Tajima region: mackerel filleted with its head and bones simmered into stock, then the flesh cooked sukiyaki-style with napa cabbage, chrysanthemum greens, and grilled tofu. It is said to have been eaten in port towns like Toyooka's Takeno, where mackerel landings were plentiful, sometimes as breakfast after a morning at sea.
source_publisher: 農林水産省「うちの郷土料理」
